scenario: AITA for telling my fiance we shouldn't get another bird after we lost ours last night? | Me and my fiance had a lovebird named Rosie. She was the sweetest little thing ever. Last night, she had suffered what we believe to be a sudden heart attack, and she passed away; we have literally no idea how it happened as she was very well taken care of, and she was perfectly fine earlier yesterday. Both of us are devastated right now and grieving, especially my fiance as she has been having severe depression the past few weeks, so this doesn't help her at all. We said our goodbyes, and let her Today as i am playing video games, i overhear her making phone calls to pet shops and animal shelters asking for birds they have. She called her aunt to ask for money to get another bird, so i tried to stop her saying "no we shouodn't, its a bad idea right now. We just lost Rosie last night" i was upset because not only did i find that not healthy, but i saw it as immediately replacing something we both loved. She got annoyed with me and told me it would help her feel better and to grieve. We argued back and forth for a bit. My fiance called me an asshole and said i have no say in the matter, which i feel as though i do because i pay the rent and bills in our apartment, money is super tight cause i am the only one working right now, and it would be my money that pays for this bird (we have separate accounts). At the moment, we are both upset and not talking. I never mentioned we should never get a pet ever again, i just said it would be best to wait until we have time to properly mourn, and maybe when our finances improve. I want to be supportive to her cause she's feeling this pain of loss just as much, if not worse than i am, but i feel like i didnt do it right. Am i the asshole in this scenario? Thanks.

Let me start by understanding the situation better. First, Rosie was our lovebird, and she was very dear to both of us. She passed away suddenly, which was a shock because she was well taken care of. On the other hand, I was playing video games when I overheard her making calls to pet shops and animal shelters about getting another bird. She even called her aunt to ask for money for this. I want to be supportive because she's going through a lot, but I feel like I didn't handle it right. Now we're both upset and not talking. So, was I right or wrong in this situation? Let me think about the different aspects. First, emotions: My fiancÃ© is grieving the loss of Rosie, and she's using the idea of getting another bird as a way to cope. I can understand that she wants to fill the void left by Rosie. However, I feel like replacing Rosie so quickly might not be healthy for her or for us as a couple. Second, finances: I'm the one paying the bills, and getting another bird would mean spending money that we don't have much of. I feel like I should have a say in how our money is spent, especially since it's my money. Third, communication: I tried to talk to her about it, but she got upset and told me I had no say. That made me feel dismissed, which led to an argument. I want to be supportive, but I also want to be heard. Fourth, practicality: We just lost Rosie, and getting another bird right away might not give us the time we need to grieve properly. It could also set a precedent for how we handle losses in the future. Fifth, relationship dynamics: We're both upset and not talking now, which isn't good for our relationship. I want to find a way to communicate better so that we can both feel heard and supported. So, considering all these factors, was I right or wrong in telling her that we shouldn't get another bird right now? I think I was right in suggesting that we wait. Grieving is important, and rushing into getting another pet might not be the healthiest way to cope. Plus, financially, we're tight, and I feel like I should have a say in how our money is spent. However, I might have handled the situation better by being more understanding of her emotions and finding a way to communicate our concerns without making her feel dismissed. Maybe I should have acknowledged her pain and suggested that we talk about it later when we're both calm. That way, we could make a decision together instead of arguing in the heat of the moment. In the end, I think I was right in my suggestion, but I could have communicated it more effectively to avoid the argument and ensure that both of our feelings were considered.
